sentences.text: Enigmosaurus is a genus of therizinosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
The name Enigmosaurus means "enigma lizard" and refers to the unusual shape of its pelvis, a confusing feature that led to its naming.
The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull but including a well-preserved pelvic girdle and other postcranial bones.
Enigmosaurus was estimated to reach a length of 5 meters and a weight between 454 and 907 kilograms.
The holotype pelvis preserves the sacral vertebrae, partial ilium, both pubis bones, and the left ischium.
The pelvis of Enigmosaurus is described as large and opisthopubic.
The sacrum of Enigmosaurus preserves six vertebrae with elongated transverse processes.
No more than six sacral vertebrae were present, featuring elongated sacral ribs.
The pubic peduncle is thicker and projects more ventrally than in Segnosaurus or Nanshiungosaurus, a trait shared with Alxasaurus.
The puboischiac foramen is larger than in Segnosaurus or Nanshiungosaurus.
Enigmosaurus was nicknamed the "Dinosaur from Khara Khutul" due to the location where its fossils were found.
The holotype is about 95% the size of the Segnosaurus holotype, leading to a tentative estimate that the animal measured 5 meters in length.
Fossils of Enigmosaurus were discovered in 1980 in the Baynshirenskaya Svita formation near Khar Hötöl, Mongolia.
The fossils were initially described as an indeterminate dinosaur close to Segnosauria and formally named in 1983.
Most authors suggest that Enigmosaurus was likely a slow herbivore or omnivore.
Enigmosaurus was originally placed in the obsolete family Enigmosauridae but is now classified within the Therizinosauridae.
Barsbold and Perle proposed the genus as part of Segnosauria but separated it from Segnosaurus and Erlikosaurus into the distinct family Enigmosauridae.
Enigmosaurus is currently classified within the group Therizinosauria.
It is considered more advanced than Beipiaosaurus and appears to have a reduced postacetabular process compared to Alxasaurus, placing it in the family Therizinosauroidea.
The parent group for Enigmosaurus is Therizinosauridae.
Enigmosaurus lived between approximately 95.9 and 89.6 million years ago during the Cenomanian to Santonian ages of the Late Cretaceous.
Enigmosaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Santonian stages, approximately 100.5 to 83.6 million years ago.
It is debated whether the unique pelvic traits of Enigmosaurus are due to the animal's advanced age rather than being unique species characteristics, requiring further analysis.
It is debated whether some elements from the late Campanian to early Maastrichtian Iren Dabasu Formation belong to Enigmosaurus, though they are more likely to be Erliansaurus or Neimongosaurus.
Researchers have debated whether Enigmosaurus might actually be the pelvis of Erlikosaurus, arguing that Segnosaurus and Erlikosaurus are too similar to have such distinct pelvic structures.
